key_terms.أَبْصَارُهَا: Eyes (plural of basar, referring to the organ of sight or faculty of vision)
key_terms.خَاشِعَةٌ: Humble, submissive, lowly (indicating modesty and reverence)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean for the eyes to be lowered in submission in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this phrase is often interpreted not merely as physical modesty but as a spiritual state of *khushu'* (humility) before Allah, reflecting the believer's constant awareness of the Divine Gaze. This concept aligns with the hadith of Imam Ali (AS) regarding the 'glance of the heart,' where inner piety dictates outward demeanor, serving as a safeguard against *ghurrah* (vanity) and *fitnah* (temptation).
